summary: Fit the straight line that makes the squared errors as small as possible.
headline: The line with the smallest squared misses
overview: Pick a line. Measure how far each dot sits above or below it. Square those misses and average them. The best line is the one with the smallest average.
Squaring means one far-off dot pulls hard on the line. That is the thing to watch when you break it.

break.label: Break it
break.explains: Add an outlier far below the pattern. The whole line tilts toward it, because a miss of 2 costs four times a miss of 1.

check.question: Why does one outlier move the fitted line so much?
options: Squared errors punish big misses heavily
The slope is always recomputed from the last point

realLife: House-price models are often fit on log prices partly so a few mansions do not drag the line.
data: Ten points that follow a gentle upward trend with a little noise. Click the plot to add more. Nothing is hidden: the same points feed the fit you see.
maths: best w, b    solve the normal equations XᵀX θ = Xᵀy
In practice the solver uses a QR factorisation instead of inverting XᵀX, which is steadier numerically.
